problem.h2: Why teams want an alternative to Burnt AI
problem.lead: Burnt calls itself an AI watchtower for food distribution and deploys agents by team: one for order intake, one for purchasing, one that calls customers about money they owe. It is a serious piece of engineering, and a Burnt AI alternative search rarely means it has failed. The question behind it is narrower: who should confirm what a kitchen asked for?

cards.h3: Software decides when a person looks
cards.body: Burnt's own page says confidence thresholds decide when human review is required. That is a sensible design, and it still means the exceptions land on your desk. Nowhere does it say the customer sees the order first.

cards.h3: A voicemail still starts as a voicemail
cards.body: Burnt transcribes what comes in by phone or as a voicemail, which is genuinely useful. But the order begins as a loose message, and the cook who left it never sees the lines your system ends up holding.

cards.h3: Agents that work are worth keeping
cards.body: If intake, purchasing and collections are already earning their keep, pulling the platform out to change who confirms an order would be a lot of disruption for one habit.

faq.h2: Burnt AI competitor, or one more step beside it?

items.q: Should I look for a Burnt AI alternative so buyers can order by speaking?
items.a: There is no need. Your Burnt agents can stay exactly as they are. VoiceOrder Solutions sits beside them as one more way in for orders: the buyer speaks it, checks it and sends it. Nothing has to be turned off.

items.q: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than Burnt AI?
items.a: On breadth, no, and it would be silly to pretend otherwise. Burnt reads channels we never touch and automates procurement and invoice chasing, which we never go near. Where we are strong is specific: the buyer approves the order, so whoever knows the kitchen settles whether it is right. If that point is why you started looking for a Burnt AI alternative, you can add it rather than swap.

items.q: Do the two products link up?
items.a: No. There is no connection between Burnt and our app, and no joint support. Their agents keep passing what they process into your system. Ours arrive separately, either emailed with a file or fed straight into your system.

items.q: Can our accounts still email or WhatsApp their orders?
items.a: Yes, and Burnt carries on reading them: it lists email, phone, voicemail, WhatsApp, SMS, EDI, portals and spreadsheets. We do not parse any inbound channel at all. A call that reaches your own desk carries no number from us, and no time stamp either: those come only with what is sent from our app.

items.q: How soon could our accounts be ordering?
items.a: Most distributors are up and running within 24 to 48 hours, and most kitchens place their first order on day one. Burnt keeps running throughout, so there is no switchover to schedule.

items.q: Will anyone need to come to our site?
items.a: Not for this. We set up from the guides you send over, with no implementation project. Burnt describes white-glove onboarding with their team working on your premises; if that already happened for your agents, adding us does not repeat it.

items.q: How is it priced if we keep Burnt?
items.a: Neither of us publishes a rate card. We quote per distributor once we know what you run, and Burnt quotes after a demo. Since the agents stay, the only figure to weigh is the price of adding our app.

items.q: Where do the Burnt details on this page come from?
items.a: Burnt's own website, read on 10 October 2026: the agent list and the on-site onboarding line off their homepage, and the channel list and the confidence-threshold wording off their sales and operations product page. We have left their accuracy and time-saving figures out, because those are their numbers to stand behind. If any of it has changed, this page is what needs correcting.
